et apotek.explanation: "Et apotek" means "a pharmacy". To say where you are going, use "på" (at): "Jeg skal på apoteket" (I have to go to the pharmacy).

et apparat.explanation: "Et apparat" means "a device". To name a specific kind of device, put a word in front: "et høreapparat" (a hearing aid).

et ar.explanation: "Et ar" means "a scar". Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year), which has a little ring over the "å". To talk about a scar: "Såret blev til et ar" (The wound became a scar). To talk about a year: "Et år har tolv måneder" (A year has twelve months).

et arbejde.explanation: "Et arbejde" means "a job / work". To say you are at your workplace, use "på arbejde" (at work): "Jeg er på arbejde" (I am at work).

et arbejdsmiljø.explanation: "Et arbejdsmiljø" means "a work environment". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "miljø" (environment). In Denmark, "Arbejdstilsynet" (the Danish Working Environment Authority) is the authority that checks the work environment.

et areal.explanation: "Et areal" means "an area", as in the size of a surface. To ask how big a room is, say: "Hvad er rummets areal?" (What is the area of the room?) Do not mix it up with "et område" (an area as a region). To talk about a region, say: "Der er mange parker i området" (There are many parks in the area).

et argument.explanation: "Et argument" means "an argument", as in a reason for your view. To ask for someone's reason, say: "Hvad er dit argument?" (What is your argument?) Do not mix it up with "et skænderi" (a quarrel). To say two people had a quarrel: "De havde et skænderi i går" (They had a quarrel yesterday).

et arkiv.explanation: "Et arkiv" means "an archive". To name what is stored, put a word in front: "et fotoarkiv" (a photo archive).

et armbåndsur.explanation: "Et armbåndsur" means "a wristwatch". It is built from "armbånd" (bracelet) and "ur" (watch or clock).

et askebæger.explanation: "Et askebæger" means "an ashtray". It ends in "bæger" (cup), as in "et æggebæger" (an egg cup).

et aspekt.explanation: "Et aspekt" means "an aspect". To say which part matters most, say: "Det vigtigste aspekt er prisen" (The most important aspect is the price).

et atom.explanation: "Et atom" means "an atom". It is the first part of "atomkraft" (nuclear power) and "atombombe" (atomic bomb).

et auditorium.explanation: "Et auditorium" means "an auditorium / lecture hall". To say where you meet for a lecture: "Vi mødes i auditoriet" (We meet in the lecture hall).

et autoværksted.explanation: "Et autoværksted" means "a car repair shop". It is built from "auto" (car) and "værksted" (workshop), which also appears in "et cykelværksted" (a bike repair shop).

at åbne.explanation: "At åbne" means "to open". To ask a shop when it opens, say: "Hvornår åbner I?" (When do you open?)

at åbne op.explanation: "At åbne op" means "to open up". When you mean to make something possible, use "åbne op for": "Det åbner op for nye muligheder" (It opens up new possibilities).

at ånde.explanation: "At ånde" means "to breathe". To say you cannot breathe, use "trække vejret" (literally, to pull the breath): "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe).

en å.explanation: "En å" means "a stream", as in flowing water. To talk about a stream: "Der er fisk i åen" (There are fish in the stream). Do not mix it up with "en flod" (a river). To talk about a big river: "Floden er meget bred" (The river is very wide).

en åbning.explanation: "En åbning" means "an opening". When you talk about the start of an event, it also means "an opening": "Åbningen af udstillingen er i morgen" (The opening of the exhibition is tomorrow).

en åbningsdag.explanation: "En åbningsdag" means "an opening day". It is built from "åbning" (opening) and "dag" (day).

en åbningstid.explanation: "En åbningstid" means "an opening hour". To ask when a shop is open, use the plural "åbningstider": "Hvad er butikkens åbningstider?" (What are the shop's opening hours?)

en åkande.explanation: "En åkande" means "a water lily". To name its leaf, add "blad" (leaf): "et åkandeblad" (a water lily leaf).

en ål.explanation: "En ål" means "an eel". Do not mix it up with "en å" (a stream). To talk about an eel: "Vi fangede en ål" (We caught an eel). To talk about a stream: "Åen er smal" (The stream is narrow).

en ånd.explanation: "En ånd" means "a spirit", as in a being without a body. When you talk about the main idea behind something, it means "the spirit": "lovens ånd" (the spirit of the law).
